approach: Revision of round 2. The shape stays: a new pure module `crates/athena-core/src/run/stale_text.rs` finds text that still says what the change made false. It runs where the decision gate already runs: once in `producer_loop` as part of the shared send-back (next to the gate, producer.rs:498-502), and at the candidate step in `check_and_verify` (after the gate block, mod.rs:2007-2020), before the pull request, the checks and the verifier. Answers to the six findings. F1: `main.rs` stays, with evidence. `lib.rs` holds no help text (lib.rs:1-68 is `hestia_report` and `age_phrase`), the strings are in `main.rs`, and criterion 5 itself asks for the diff 'of the file where each such constant and string live'. Criterion 9 conflicts with that, so one `User:` question remains. F2: the value match is tightened to prose with the value next to a word of the constant's name (decision 3). A small number needs two name words. A value that matches more than 6 places becomes advisory (printed, never closing, like the gate's notes at checks.rs:716-718). New tests use a real-shaped `REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS` 3 to 4 change over unrelated '3 jobs' lines. F3: in the reading, `from A to B` needs numbers or quoted strings, and a decision is named only as the object of a reversal verb (decision 2). Bare 'replace(s)' and 'no longer' are dropped as triggers. F4: the reason for rule (a) is corrected (decision 4). F5: the self-trip risk is dropped; the producer instead greps its own replaced lines by hand. F6: the second tree build is accepted and stated, because avoiding it needs a `snapshot.rs` edit that is not a deliverable. One more conflict found while re-reading: `producer_loop` limits a job to its allowed paths (producer.rs:325-334, :493-495), so a stale place in a file the job may not edit cannot be fixed in the loop. The loop adapter does not send such places back; the candidate step still closes the job with them named (decision 6). Help strings keep D156's `{placeholder}` mechanism (main.rs:602-623), extended by a generic `fill_limits` in lib.rs. The change is recorded as D190 (appended, `Amends D156`, link D156 to D190) and one CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: 1. Hook the check at the two places the decision gate already uses. One pure function `stale_text::check` serves both adapters. `Athena::stale_text_in_snapshot` is called in `producer_loop` next to the gate (producer.rs:498-502). It is skipped when `self.nested.is_some()` or `changes.is_empty()`. It reads the snapshot's own git, `snapshot.base()` and `snapshot.work_tree_tree()`. `Athena::stale_text_at_candidate` is a new block after mod.rs:2020 with the same guards (`recorded_checks.is_none() && self.nested.is_none()`) and the same closing handling as mod.rs:2013-2019. It reads `self.git` with the base commit `p` and candidate commit `c`. Both take `accepted` (producer.rs:302; mod.rs:1961).
decisions.reason: This is the shape for a finding that must reach the producer inside its loop and still stop the job before the verifier: `unreconciled_in_snapshot` (checks.rs:734) is called at producer.rs:498 and `unreconciled_decisions` (checks.rs:697) at mod.rs:2013. The closing uses `Athena::failure`. `StopCause::of` (disk.rs:462) classes a reason with no environment prefix as Work, so the job is not held as an environment stop. The pinned-run guard of `run_loop_checks` (checks.rs:450) is not copied because this check builds nothing. The nested guard is kept because the outer job sees the combined change. Cost (F6): `change_list` already calls `work_tree_tree()` (snapshot.rs:200-207), so the adapter builds the tree a second time per pass (one `git add -A` and `write-tree` in a temporary index, snapshot.rs:210-218). It is accepted. Removing it needs a `change_list` change in `crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs`, which D08 governs (decision-links.toml:196-201) and which is not a deliverable. The adapter runs only when there are changes.

rejected.option: Run it only inside `run_loop_checks` (checks.rs:444)
rejected.why: That run is advisory and is skipped for low disk, a busy slot, tool configuration and a pinned run (checks.rs:450-464). A skipped run would let stale text reach the verdict.

rejected.option: Run it only at the candidate
rejected.why: The producer would see the list only on a retry; the request asks for the list inside the producer's own loop.

rejected.option: Add it to the verifier's gap list
rejected.why: That is a model's judgement, so the rule would be prose, against the mechanism default.

rejected.option: Compute the tree once in `producer_loop` and pass it to both `change_list` and the check (F6 option)
rejected.why: `change_list` takes no tree argument. Re-implementing its body in `producer_loop` duplicates it, and changing it edits snapshot.rs, a D08-governed file outside the deliverables.

decisions.choice: 2. Needles come from five sources, each narrow. (1) Diff values: in one file a removed and an added `const`/`static NAME: T = LIT;` with the same NAME and different single literals. A literal is one unsigned number or one string of at least 3 characters. Old = the removed literal, new = the added one. Keywords are the lowercase parts of NAME minus GENERIC (max, min, limit, default, value, count, number, size, total, num) and minus parts of 2 characters or fewer. (2) Reading values: a sentence of the accepted reading (summary, assumptions, criteria; split at '. ', '; ' and newlines) with `from A to B` where A and B are each an unsigned number or a double-quoted string, AND a named identifier in the same sentence (SCREAMING_SNAKE, or a backticked word with no '/', '.' or space). Old = A; keywords come from that identifier. Words as A or B (`from main to athena/records`, `from the base to the candidate`) make no needle. (3) Reading claims: a double-quoted or backticked span of 6 or more words within 40 characters after `no longer`, `instead of`, `rather than`, `replaces`, `reverses` or `used to say`. (4) Reading decisions: a decision id as the OBJECT of a reversal verb: `(reverses|reversing|supersedes|superseding|overturns|overturning|reverts) [decision ]D<nn>`, or `D<nn> (no longer holds|no longer stands|no longer applies|is reversed|is superseded|is overturned)`. Bare `replace(s)` and a bare `no longer` elsewhere in the sentence are not triggers. The needle is reported only when that heading exists in the base log and the entry is not marked (decision 4), at its heading line. (5) Diff claims: from replaced hunks only (decision 5).
decisions.reason: The request says 'a job's reading or diff', and the accepted reading's assumption says old values come 'from removed diff lines ... and from decision-style claims in the reading'. The reading is at both call sites. Answers F3: form (2) takes only literals as old and new, so a sentence with words after `from` is quiet; form (4) fires only when the id is what the verb acts on, so 'D156's placeholder replaces the literal' and 'follows D156' are quiet. Requiring an identifier keeps this job's own criterion text ('a constant changes from 8 to 16') from becoming a needle, since it holds no identifier. A reversal that the reading words in another way is not caught; D190's Tradeoff says so.

rejected.option: Ignore the reading (round 1)
rejected.why: A job whose reading reverses a rule but whose diff has no replaced line would find nothing.

rejected.option: Take every number of the reading as an old value
rejected.why: Most numbers in a reading are criteria counts and file sizes.

rejected.option: `from X to Y` with any words as X and Y (round 2)
rejected.why: 'moves `records` from main to athena/records' would make 'main' a needle.

rejected.option: A cited decision id plus replace(s) or 'no longer' anywhere in the sentence (round 2)
rejected.why: It fires on citations; the producer would then write a bogus 'Amends Dn in prose only' entry, the failure D187 refused (decisions.md:5502-5503).

rejected.option: Make decision hits from the reading send-back-only
rejected.why: An explicit reading statement that a decision is reversed, with no mark, is the case the request names. With the object-of-verb form it is narrow enough to close on.

decisions.choice: 3. A value hit is prose with the old value next to a word of the name (answers F2). Hit = a line i of a searched file, not a line the diff added, that meets all of: (a) the old value is a whole token: no letter, digit or '_' touches it and no '.' joins it to a digit; (b) the line does not hold the new value as a whole token; (c) the old value and a keyword stand in one plain-word run, at most WINDOW_WORDS = 4 words apart. A plain-word run is a maximal stretch of letters, digits, spaces, commas, hyphens and apostrophes. Any other character ends a run: '(' ')' '=' ';' '_' ':' '.' '`' '"' and operators. Keywords match in lowercase and ignore a trailing 's'. (d) When the old value is a single digit (0-9) and the name has two or more keywords, two different keywords occur within lines i-2..=i+2. Code is not prose, so `assert_eq!(jobs.len(), 3)` and `let n = 3;` never match. Firm and advisory: a value needle with more than FIRM_VALUE_HITS = 6 hits makes all its hits advisory. They are printed as `stale text  note:` lines (at most 5), never put in the brief and never closing. Claim and decision hits are always firm. The module's `Report` has `firm` and `advisory`.
decisions.reason: I re-measured the finding's claim with the real constants: IMPROVEMENT_GAP=2 (plan.rs:466), HOLD_ATTEMPTS=2 (scope_guard.rs:80), LOW_RATING=2 (audience.rs:37), REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS=3 (plan.rs:471), BACKFILL_HIGH=5 (hestia.rs:1494). All are small numbers whose name words (jobs, urgent, attempts) are common in the repository. Adjacency in a plain run removes code lines and distant words. The two-word rule for single digits removes '3 jobs' lines that never mention the other name words. The breaker means a needle that still matches broadly cannot close a job. The remaining false-positive mode is a single-digit value, a one-word name and fewer than 7 prose hits, such as `MAX_JOBS` 3 to 4 with a few unrelated '3 jobs' sentences. D190's Tradeoff says so. A restatement that names only one of two name words beside a single digit is missed, as is a number spelled out in words. A stale place in `docs/design/*.md` is searched like any other.

rejected.option: Round 2's rule: the old value as a whole token on a line that shares any keyword
rejected.why: Hundreds of '3 jobs' and '1 producer' lines match, mostly in code, tests and old decisions.

rejected.option: Search only doc comments, help strings and .md prose through a Rust parser
rejected.why: Help text is a multi-line string literal (main.rs:295-323) and a string-state scanner is a new parser with its own faults. The plain-run rule gets the same effect from the characters of the line.

rejected.option: Require the line to name the constant or its exact phrase
rejected.why: A help string restates a limit in words ('at most 8 widgets'), not by the constant's name; it would miss the case the request names.

rejected.option: Close only on a stricter rule and make every other value hit send-back-only
rejected.why: A send-back-only hit would spend a whole producer run on text that may be unrelated. The breaker plus the stricter rule gives the same safety with one tier of consequences.

decisions.choice: 4. 'Marked' (answers F4). A decision entry (from its `## D<n> ` heading to the next `## ` heading) is marked when: (a) its text holds `amended by D<nn>` or `superseded by D<nn>`, any case, with an id of at least two digits ('amended by hand' marks nothing); or (b) the new `docs/decision-links.toml` has a `[[link]]` with `older` = the id and `status = "superseded"`; or (c) it has a `[[link]]` with `older` = the id whose `newer` heading is not in the base log, so this change reconciles it itself. A link whose `newer` already stood at the base and whose status is `amended` marks nothing, because the header says the older decision 'stays active' (decision-links.toml:5-6). Outside the log, a blank-line paragraph is marked when it holds the same phrase followed by a `D<nn>` id, a backticked name or a path with an extension. The status is read with `toml_edit::DocumentMut` (a dependency of athena-core, Cargo.toml:26), because `link_pairs` (decision_links.rs:101) drops it. A links text that does not parse marks nothing. CHANGELOG.md, `records/`, `target/` and `.git/` are never searched.
decisions.reason: The request exempts text 'marked amended by or superseded by'. Correction of the round 2 reason: `parse_supersessions` reads the phrases 'superseded by', 'supersedes' and 'amends' (decision_links.rs:254-258), not 'amended by'. 'Superseded by D<nn>' inside an older entry is the form that `parse_supersessions` and `link_problems` already pair with a link. 'Amended by D<nn>' is a mark only this check reads, kept because the request names it. The log is append-only, so no old entry of this repository can gain either phrase; they mark an entry only where it already stands (4 'superseded by D<nn>' phrases in decisions.md today) or an entry this change adds. In this repository the links list is how a supersession is recorded: 29 `[[link]]` tables, of which 1 has status superseded and 28 amended. Counting any `older` id as marked would exempt D08 and D156, the two decisions that motivated this job, because D157, D160 and D171 amend D08 and D187 amends D156. Rule (c) is the route the gate already teaches (checks.rs:94-97: `Amends <id> in prose only` plus a link).

rejected.option: Any `older` id of any link is marked (round 1)
rejected.why: It never reports a contradiction of D08 or D156.

rejected.option: Count the bare words 'amended by' anywhere in the entry
rejected.why: 'The list is amended by hand' would exempt a whole entry.

rejected.option: Reuse `link_pairs` for the marks
rejected.why: It returns pairs without status.

decisions.choice: 5. Claims come only from lines the change replaces. Hunks are read with `git diff -U0 --no-color --no-renames --no-ext-diff <from> <to>` through the public `Git::run_bytes` (athena-git lib.rs:259; `added_lines` at lib.rs:642 uses the same command). A hunk with both removed and added lines is a replacement. A hunk with only removed lines (a deleted function, a deleted paragraph, a deleted file whose `+++` is `/dev/null`) yields no claim. A removed line must have 6 or more words (MIN_CLAIM_WORDS) and be a comment or prose line (`//`, `///`, `//!`, `#` in toml, a non-table line of `.md`), and must not reappear as an added line anywhere in the diff, so a moved comment is quiet. A claim hit is the claim's words (case, punctuation and line wraps ignored) as a contiguous run in a searched file.
decisions.reason: A deleted function or file is not a reversed claim, and a hard failure forces a bogus entry. Replacement hunks are what an edit of a stated behaviour looks like, and `-U0` hunks give that pairing without writing a diff algorithm. The finding text names the honest escape for a false hit in an old decision: an entry that says `Amends D<n> in prose only` with an `amended` link (checks.rs:94-97).

rejected.option: Every removed comment or prose line is a claim (round 1)
rejected.why: Deleting a function would fail any job that leaves a copy of its comment elsewhere.

rejected.option: A line-level LCS diff inside the module
rejected.why: New algorithm and tests; `git diff -U0` gives the hunks.

decisions.choice: 6. Exits of the new stage, one line each. PASS (no firm findings): both adapters return empty (new call next to producer.rs:498; new block after mod.rs:2020 falls through); the loop's all-clear test (producer.rs:545-556) gains `stale.is_empty()`; no state is left; the verifier path reads next. ADVISORY ONLY (value needle over 6 hits): `stale text  note:` UI lines, nothing else; same as PASS. FAIL with a send-back left: `send_backs += 1` (producer.rs:676-677); `stale text left where the change makes it false: <n> place(s)` joins `problems` (producer.rs:557-613); `append_stale_text` is applied last to `attempt_brief` (producer.rs:701-712); the brief is the state, read by the next producer pass, which reruns the check. FAIL at the limit (`send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, producer.rs:635-675): print `producer   stale text still left after the send-back; the job ends before the verifier` and break with the report; the list is not added to `report_problems` (producer.rs:583); the work tree keeps the text, which the candidate step reads next. FAIL at the candidate: the block after mod.rs:2020 sets `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &reason)` with `stale text left by the change: <list>`, keeping `changed_paths` and `verification_passed = None` as at mod.rs:2014-2018, and returns; the Failed outcome is the state that close and the records read, and `athena retry` starts a fresh producer whose loop reruns the check. STALE PLACE OUTSIDE THE ALLOWED PATHS (job has a limiting criterion): the loop adapter drops findings whose path `outside_allowed_paths(allowed, ..)` (mod.rs:1745) returns, because the producer may not edit them and a send-back would waste a producer run; the candidate adapter keeps them, so the job fails with those places named. ERROR (diff, tree or blob read fails): both adapters return empty and print `producer   stale text not checked: <why>`, the policy of `settle_loop_checks` (checks.rs:432-441) that an advisory read failure never discards finished work; no state is left. HOLD: cannot happen; the check takes no slot and reads no disk gate. INTERRUPT: cannot happen inside the check (bounded git reads, no agent or process wait); the kill switch is read by the producer invocation before it and by `refuse_if_stopped` at the next stage. SKIPPED without a line: `self.nested.is_some()`, an empty change list, `recorded_checks.is_some()` (a resume at the verifier stage), no base commit in the snapshot, no needles.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for every exit of a new stage; each row names the file:line that handles it, the state it leaves and the code that reads that state next. PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS is 1 (mod.rs:1682) and SCOPE_SEND_BACKS is 1 (mod.rs:1735), so a stale finding uses the shared slot, as the gate does.

rejected.option: Treat a read error as a finding
rejected.why: A git read failure says nothing about the work; it would fail jobs for the environment.

rejected.option: Send back places outside the allowed paths
rejected.why: The producer may not edit them (scope send-back, producer.rs:633-634), so the pass would be wasted.

rejected.option: Drop out-of-scope places at the candidate too
rejected.why: A change that makes text false and cannot fix it would then land with the text false, which is what the request ends.

decisions.choice: 7. Help strings (answers the round 2 findings F5 and F8, unchanged). A doc comment is a literal, so `format!` or `concat!` cannot take a constant there; D156's `{placeholder}` fill (main.rs:602-623, test `drain_help_follows_the_ceiling_it_is_built_from` near main.rs:1511) is the existing, tested way. A generic `athena_cli::fill_limits(command, &[(name, value)])` runs once over the whole tree in `cli_command()` (main.rs:612) and replaces `{name}` in about, long about, before and after help and each arg's help and long help. Conversions (all constants are already `pub`): `plan` main.rs:350-355 'default 3 urgent, 10 high' from `DEFAULT_URGENT_CAP`, `DEFAULT_HIGH_CAP` (config.rs:54,56); 'one dispatch in three' from `IMPROVEMENT_GAP + 1` (plan.rs:466); 'three or more distinct jobs' from `REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS` (plan.rs:471). `drain` after_help: :321 'at most two other items' from `IMPROVEMENT_GAP`; :323 'three or more distinct jobs' from `REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS`; :295 'two attempts that did not land' from `athena_core::scope_guard::HOLD_ATTEMPTS` (scope_guard.rs:80); :307 'default 1' from `athena_data::config::Parallel::default().max_concurrency` (config.rs:291-297). `check` main.rs:487 'pending for 15 minutes' from `athena_gate::attribution::PENDING_WINDOW` (attribution.rs:52). Hestia `review` main.rs:573-574 'five highest-ranked causes ... are urgent' from `athena_core::hestia::BACKFILL_HIGH` (hestia.rs:1494), with 'urgent' corrected to 'high' as the constant's doc and its use say. `audience` main.rs:147 'A rating of 2 or lower' from `athena_core::audience::LOW_RATING` (audience.rs:37). Rating '1 to 5' at main.rs:147, 336 and 400 from `athena_data::records::RATING_RANGE` (work.rs:181); the two `value_parser!(u8).range(1..=5)` at main.rs:337 and 401 become one `rating_parser()` that reads the same constant. Not converted, with reasons: 'every 30 seconds' (main.rs:370) is a literal `Duration::from_secs(30)` with no constant; 'failed twice' (main.rs:279-281) is the private `ATTEMPTS` (drain.rs:324) and a quoted report reason that tests/drain.rs asserts; 'two thirds' (main.rs:72) is `rows.len() * 2 / 3` with no constant; 'two separate git worktrees' (main.rs:176) describes a method; display.rs:705 is report output and a file outside the deliverables, named in D190's Tradeoff as a follow-up.
decisions.reason: This keeps D156's mechanism and its test, converts every help string that restates a limit that has an enforcing constant, and makes help and parser read one constant so they cannot drift. `main.rs` is needed: lib.rs holds no help text (lib.rs:1-68) and `cli_command()` and the derive text live in main.rs.

rejected.option: The `const_format` crate for `concat!`
rejected.why: It changes Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, and a derive doc comment cannot take it.

rejected.option: Convert only `plan`, `drain` and `check` (round 1)
rejected.why: It misses the Hestia review (already stale: 'urgent' against `BACKFILL_HIGH`), the audience low rating and the rating range.

rejected.option: Make `default_max_concurrency`, `ATTEMPTS` or the 30-second wait public
rejected.why: It edits athena-data/config.rs and drain.rs, outside the listed files, and 'failed twice' is asserted as a report string. `Parallel::default()` already exposes the first.

rejected.option: Do the whole help override from lib.rs and leave main.rs alone (F1)
rejected.why: The literal doc comments would stay in main.rs, so the old numbers would remain in help text and criterion 5 ('no literal copy of the limit remains') would fail; `cli_command()` in main.rs must also call the fill.

decisions.choice: 8. Record as a new entry D190, appended after D189 (decisions.md:5580), heading `## D190 · ` with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and a Provenance bullet. The Decision says `Amends D156` for the part it extends: D156's rule that help text states a limit from the constant that enforces it, now for more strings, and D156's alternative (d), a send-back of a finding inside the loop, now for stale text. It adds one `[[link]]` older = D156, newer = D190, status = amended. It claims only what D187 already did: `decision_gate` runs in the producer loop and again at the candidate (decisions.md:5487; producer.rs:498). It does not claim to end D156's remark that the finding reaches the producer on the next attempt for governed paths, and it names D187's open follow-ups (decisions.md:5506-5509) as untouched. The Tradeoff states: textual match only; claims from replaced hunks only; the value rule's remaining false-positive mode (single-digit value, one-word name, fewer than 7 prose hits) and its misses (one of two name words beside a single digit, numbers spelled out, reworded reversals); the advisory tier; the escape for a false hit in an old decision (`Amends D<n> in prose only` plus an `amended` link); a stale place outside a job's allowed paths ends the job; the retry brief does not carry the list; display.rs:705 left literal. No link to D187. No existing entry is edited.
decisions.reason: A phrase `Amends D156` needs a matching link, or the gate holds the job (checks.rs:100-117 `link_problems`; `link_problem_sentence` at checks.rs:28-55). The log is append-only (mirrors.rs `decision log` AppendOnly), and `decision entries` needs the heading and a Provenance bullet (mirrors.rs:71-74). The refusal-rate figure in the brief is an estimate and goes in neither D190 nor the CHANGELOG.

rejected.option: Write no phrase and add no link
rejected.why: The change extends D156; an entry that hides that leaves the log contradicting itself, which is what this check exists to stop.

rejected.option: Also link D187
rejected.why: This change finishes none of D187's follow-ups; a link without a phrase fails `link_problems`.

decisions.choice: 9. Matching-rule forms and the refusal corpus. The check is not a reading check and adds no reading refusal, so it does not enter `refusing_check` (reading/checks.rs:520), which `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` reads (refusal_corpus.rs:2905). The corpus builders (`reading_check_cases`, refusal_corpus.rs:1993) run `check_reading` over a stored reading, and this rule runs over a diff, a tree and the reading as input, so no existing case id maps to these forms and a new corpus case would test nothing. The forms are covered by `stale_text` unit tests: a single-number const; a single-string const; a const with two literals (skipped); a const with only generic name words (skipped); the small-value two-word rule; `from 8 to 16` with a SCREAMING_SNAKE identifier; the same with a backticked identifier; the same with no identifier (no needle); `from main to athena/records` and `from the base to the candidate` (no needle); a quoted old claim after each marker; a quoted span under 6 words (no claim); `reverses D45`, `supersedes D45`, `D45 no longer holds` (needle); `D156's placeholder replaces the literal` and `follows D156` (no needle); a heading id absent from the log (ignored); each marking form (a)-(c) and a base-standing `amended` link; a claim wrapped over two lines; a deleted function and a deleted file; a moved comment; a CHANGELOG.md line; a line added by the diff; code lines with the old value; a value with 7 hits (advisory).
decisions.reason: The task template asks for the input forms of a matching rule and their corpus cases. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is still run as a regression demonstration that no reading outcome changed; I cite no result.

rejected.option: Add refusal-corpus cases for the stale-text forms
rejected.why: The corpus cannot produce an outcome for a rule over a diff and a tree.

files.purpose: The pure check: `Hunk`, `Input`, `Stale` (Display `path:line (D<id>): still says <what> (<why>): <text>`), `Report { firm, advisory }`, constants (`MIN_CLAIM_WORDS` = 6, `WINDOW_WORDS` = 4, `FIRM_VALUE_HITS` = 6, `MAX_LISTED` = 30, `STALE_REASON_PREFIX`); needle extractors; the plain-run value match; the marked-entry rule with link status read by `toml_edit`; the search and the added-line exemption; `read_diff`, `read_files`, `check`; and the unit tests for criteria 1-3.
Declare `mod stale_text;` and add the candidate-step block after the decision gate (after line 2020) that closes the job with the stale-text reason.

Call `stale_text_in_snapshot` in `producer_loop` beside the decision gate, passing `scope` for the allowed-path filter, and add its findings to the all-clear test, the problem list, the limit-reached line and the send-back brief.

Add `Athena::stale_text_in_snapshot` and `Athena::stale_text_at_candidate`, the two adapters over `stale_text::check`; both take the accepted reading, print advisory notes, and print a skip line on a read error.

risks.risk: False positives: an unrelated prose line holds the old value beside a word of the name, or a replaced line's words survive in a document. A hard failure at the candidate then forces a producer to write an 'Amends Dn in prose only' entry for an old decision it did not change. The remaining value mode is a single-digit value, a one-word name and fewer than 7 prose hits (for example `MAX_JOBS` 3 to 4 with a few unrelated '3 jobs' sentences).
risks.mitigation: Value hits need prose (a plain-word run), the old value within 4 words of a name word, two name words for a single digit, and no new value on the line; a value with more than 6 hits is advisory and never closes. Claims come only from replaced hunks, need 6 or more words and a whole-line word run, and must not be re-added. Reading values need numeric or quoted ends and a named identifier; reading decisions need a reversal verb whose object is the id. Output is capped at 30 findings plus a count. The finding text names the escape (`Amends D<n> in prose only` with an `amended` link, checks.rs:94-97). Tests cover the real-shaped REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS case, the breaker, a non-matching 8, a moved comment, a deleted function and a deleted file. The refusal rate is the brief's estimate, not measured.

risks.risk: Reading every text file of the tree on each producer pass costs time and memory on a large repository, and the loop adapter builds the work-tree tree a second time per pass (F6).
risks.mitigation: The tree is read only when the diff or reading yields a needle. Only `.rs .md .toml .yml .yaml .sh` files of at most 2 MiB are read; CHANGELOG.md, `records/`, `target/` and `.git/` are skipped; blobs are read in chunks of 200 with one `cat-file --batch` (`cat_blobs`, athena-git lib.rs:988) after `blob_sizes` (:966). The extra tree build is one `git add -A` and `write-tree` in a temporary index (snapshot.rs:210-218), done once per pass and only when there are changes; the cost is accepted because removing it means editing snapshot.rs, which D08 governs. A failed read is a skip line, not a failure.

risks.risk: A decision that restates the old rule in other words is missed, as is a reading that words a reversal differently, a value spelled in words, and a restatement that names one of two name words beside a single digit. A heading that moves is re-keyed by id, not line.
risks.mitigation: The brief puts semantic matching out of scope. The wrap-tolerant word-run match and the entry/paragraph rule are covered by tests with a wrapped sentence and with the marking forms. D190's Tradeoff says reworded reversals and the other misses are not caught.

risks.risk: The new decision entry or the CHANGELOG entry trips the ontology rule, the append-only rule or the banned-word scan.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` and `cargo test -p xtask` after writing D190. D190 contains no ontology term definition and is appended at the end of the file.

risks.risk: A clap doc comment is stored as `about` or `long_about` depending on its paragraphs, and an arg's text as `help` or `long_help`, so a fill that reads the wrong getter leaves a placeholder in the help.
risks.mitigation: `fill_limits` fills whichever of about, long about, before and after help and each arg's help or long help exists, over every subcommand, and the criterion 5 test asserts no `{` survives in the rendered help of each converted command. clap is 4.6.7 (Cargo.lock:249-251); if `mut_subcommands` or `mut_args` is missing, use `mut_subcommand` per name. If `jiff::SignedDuration::as_mins` is missing, use `as_secs() / 60` for `PENDING_WINDOW`.

risks.mitigation: The retry's own producer loop reruns the check and supplies the list in its first send-back (shown by the loop test); stated in D190's Tradeoff.

risks.risk: A job with a limiting criterion has a stale place in a file it may not edit: the producer cannot fix it, and the candidate closes the job.

(5) Quiet tests for F3: `D156's placeholder replaces the literal`, `follows D156`, `moves `records` from main to athena/records`, `diff `Snapshot` from the base to the candidate`, and `from 8 to 16` with no identifier. demonstrations.observes: An unmarked decision is named by id and line; marked entries and decisions that stand are treated as the rule says; a changed rule that exists only in the reading is found; wording that states no reversal is quiet.

If marking were ignored or too loose the quiet-variant assertions fail; if too strict the unmarked assertions fail. The reading-only test fails if the reading is not read: its diff has no removed line. The F3 quiet tests fail under round 2's looser forms.

demonstrations.method: Three tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. `stale_text_is_sent_back_to_the_producer_before_verification`: a repository with `src/limits.rs` (`MAX_WIDGETS: u32 = 8`) and `HELP.md` (`at most 8 widgets`); an `editing`-style script sets the constant to 16 and records prompts; assert prompts[1] holds `## Sent back`, the heading `Stale text`, `HELP.md:1` and the old value, the UI line `producer   sent back: stale text left where the change makes it false`, and counts (2, 1) with the job landing once the script fixes HELP.md on the send-back. `stale_text_left_after_the_send_back_ends_the_job_before_the_verifier`: a script that never fixes HELP.md; assert state Failed, reason starting `stale text left by the change:` and naming `HELP.md:1`, counts (2, 0), no `checks     ` or `verifier   ` line, the line `producer   stale text still left after the send-back; the job ends before the verifier`, and `!crate::disk::is_environment_reason(&done.reason)`. `stale_text_outside_the_allowed_paths_is_not_sent_back_and_ends_the_job`: the reading limits files to `src/limits.rs`; the stale `HELP.md` is not sent back (producer count 1) and the job fails at the candidate naming `HELP.md:1`.
